text:
Alex: quick check — I rolled a tiny terraform change in staging: inference service port moved from 8080 -> 80 to align with the new sidecar, and now NLB health checks are flapping. can someone sanity-check svc/gateway tls mapping?

Priya: @Alex can you paste the Service YAML + the terraform diff for the service resource? also which gateway listener mode are we using (TLS TERMINATE vs PASSTHROUGH)? :eyes: 

Alex: putting snippets below. listener is TLS PASSTHROUGH on the inference gateway.

Alex: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
  namespace: staging
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-protocol: "TCP"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port: "traffic-port"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Cluster
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
      protocol: TCP
  selector:
    app: inference
```

Alex: terraform diff (only service_port change):

```diff
- port = 8080
+ port = 80
```

Jamie: likely cause — NLB healthcheck in passthrough mode expects to probe the nodePort/instance port (traffic-port). since you changed the service port to 80 but targetPort is still 8080, the container is listening on 8080 and healthchecks hitting 80 -> 80 gets TCP reset. two options:
- make Service port match container (set port: 8080) so traffic-port probes map to listening socket
- or update the aws-load-balancer-healthcheck-port to the nodePort number (explicit) so NLB probes your targetPort.

Jamie: also consider externalTrafficPolicy: Local if you want node-level instance healthchecks to reflect actual pod readiness and preserve source IP for security rules. with Cluster the health check may hit a node without pod and fail.

Priya: +1 on changing extTrafficPolicy to Local for staging while we debug. also double-check gateway TLS mode: PASSTHROUGH means TLS terminates at pod, so the backend must present the cert or accept TLS. if you hoped to let the gateway terminate TLS, that mismatch will break things.

Ryan: small note on Gateway API mapping — if the Gateway listener TLS mode is PASSTHROUGH we do NOT attach the TLS secret to the Gateway listener; the backend pod must have the cert or handle TLS. If you want ALB-like termination, change listener tls.mode to TERMINATE and attach secretRef. Right now with NLB passthrough + service port change you might be probing the wrong port/protocol.

Alex: ok that makes sense. quick question: is the healthcheck-port annotation the right way to set probe to 8080 or should we change service.port instead?

Jamie: either works. I prefer making Service.port == containerPort for clarity (port: 8080, targetPort: 8080). annotations are finicky across controllers. if you rely on traffic-port semantics everywhere, use the annotation.

Priya: example minimal fix I pushed locally:
```yaml
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
    - name: tls-passthrough
      port: 8080
      targetPort: 8080
      protocol: TCP
```

Priya: and terraform revert to port = 8080 for the k8s_service resource.

Alex: deploying that now to staging… will report back. infra-bot: kick a probe? :pray:

infra-bot: deploy pipeline triggered for staging/inference-svc (build #342). healthcheck monitor enabled.

Alex: staging looks green after the revert + externalTrafficPolicy=Local change. NLB healthchecks are steady and pods are receiving TLS passthrough connections. :thumbsup:

Ryan: awesome — follow up items: make a note in the terraform module docs that for TLS PASSTHROUGH services we prefer service.port == containerPort, and add a test case for extTrafficPolicy=Local with NLB.

Priya: will add a short note in infra runbook + open a tiny PR to the TF module with a doc block.

Alex: thanks all. closing the loop — will roll the TF rollback to prod tomorrow during the maintenance window. :white_check_mark:
